description: Peak dedicated graphics memory of one stable-diffusion.cpp process generating one Iris-3B image under different --max-vram budgets.
runner: stable-diffusion.cpp master-f5df5f8, Vulkan build for Windows (sd-master-f5df5f8-bin-win-vulkan-x64)
method: The Windows 'GPU Process Memory' dedicated-usage counter for the runner's process, sampled about once per second. Other applications are excluded. Sub-second peaks can be missed, and the figure includes the driver's per-process allocations. One run per row.
output_comparison: For this prompt, the images from budgets 3, 3 with batched guidance off, and 2 were pixel-identical to the 16 GiB image (mean absolute difference 0 of 255). This is one prompt and seed and does not establish identical output in general.
limits: Only the Vulkan runner build was measured; a CUDA build was not.
--max-vram is a budget for managed weights and runner buffers, not a hard cap; the measured peaks are the evidence.
A smaller budget streams weights and cuts the graph into segments, so generation is slower (about three to four times here).
